videos.caption: #recipeideas #gelatin  Gelatin is collagen just in a different form. Collagen is a structural protein found in animal tissues like skin, bones, and connective tissue. When you take that collagen and cook it (heat + water), it breaks down into gelatin. What actually happens: 	•	Collagen has a tight, triple-helix structure (very strong and rigid) 	•	When heated, that structure unwinds and partially breaks down 	•	This creates a softer, more digestible form → gelatin So when you see: “Unflavored natural gelatin (bovine)” 	•	“Bovine” = comes from cows 	•	“Unflavored” = no additives 	•	“Gelatin” = collagen that has been hydrolyzed by heat

THE ONE YOU’VE ALL BEEN WAITING FOR: COLLAGEN CHAT (Girl Science Edition) 🩷 First up, collagen is important. It’s what keeps your skin bouncy, joints cushioned, and tissues strong. Your body makes collagen, but rom your mid-20s, that production starts to dip – and drops faster post-menopause thanks to hormonal changes. DO YOU NEED TO TAKE A COLLAGEN SUPPLEMENT? Collagen supplements don’t “top up” your collagen directly. They’re broken down into small peptides that signal your body to make more, but only if your body’s in the right state to respond. That generally comes from you sleeping well, eating a balanced diet with enough protein and managing your stress, Without those foundations, the signal’s weak – and your collagen powder probably won’t do much. Where collagen actually delivers: 💞Joints: Hydrolysed or type II collagen can help reduce joint pain and slow cartilage breakdown (especially if osteoarthritis runs in your family). 🌟Skin: Evidence is mixed. High-quality, independent studies show minimal benefit for elasticity or hydration. 💅Hair & nails: Not much science here yet. Takehome message: collagen can support you, but it’s not a miracle. Focus on your foundations first – balanced nutrition, sleep, and stress management – and collagen becomes the cherry on top, not the whole sundae 🍒 #collagen #collagenforwomen #girlscience #womenshealth #hormonehealth

Patients ask me about collagen supplements every week! If you take collagen peptides, you probably want to know what effect it is having on your skin. Well..... drumroll.... We now have a meta-analysis of 35 randomised controlled trials, over 2,500 people, published in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology. The effect on dermal density, (the actual structure of your skin) does not change - it has NO EFFECT ON WRINKLES. The authors put it plainly: those apparent benefits seen previously were "attributable to statistical artifacts rather than genuine treatment effects" - not real, in other words. And dose and type didn't matter. Higher doses did not reliably produce better results. The relationship was described as chaotic. It did show the skin can be more hydrated and increased elasticity but remember, hydration is the easiest outcome in dermatology to shift. A basic moisturiser does it in an hour. So this study shows that Collagen Supplementation is working like a moisturiser. If you enjoy yours and you know what you're buying, carry on. But hopefully we can stop seeing these wrinkle claims everywhere or some good well conducted studies to show us otherwise. References: A. Batool, M. S. Abbas, R. Farooq, et al., " Oral Collagen Peptides and Skin Rejuvenation: A Systematic Review and an Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials," Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology 25, no. 7(2026): e71041, https://doi.org/10.1111/jocd.71041.
